Subject: MSA redlines - output ownership & training prohibition

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. As part of our procurement review we've attached our proposed redlines to the MSA and Order Form. Two key asks from Vellum: 1) Customer must own the Outputs (including derivatives) produced by Redwood's models when using our prompts/data, and 2) Redwood may not use Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve models (no training use) without our explicit written consent.

We understand you may want a feedback license for quality/safety, but we need it tightly constrained (timebound, no model training, limited to aggregated/anonymized telemetry). Please review and let us know where Redwood can compromise.

Hi Sara — thanks for the detailed notes and redlines. We're aligned on the goal: strong customer control over their data and outputs. Looping in Marissa (sales) and Karthik (legal) to coordinate the trade-offs.

Quick summary of our position so you have transparency from the outset:
- Customer ownership of Outputs: Redwood is generally comfortable with language that makes clear customers have rights to the content generated from their inputs. We want to avoid language that tries to limit Redwood's ability to provide the service (e.g., claims that outputs are "exclusive" if they conflict with product telemetry).
- Training prohibition: Redwood can accept a prohibition on using raw Customer Data/Outputs to train models without consent. We typically propose a narrow feedback license for safety and product improvement that excludes training on identifiable customer data and permits use of aggregated, de-identified signals.

I've attached our draft MSA_v3_redlines.pdf with inline suggestions — highlights are: a definition for "Outputs", a definition for "Customer Feedback", an explicit prohibition on model training without consent, and a carve-out for anonymized aggregate telemetry for service improvement.

Can we schedule a short call this week with your legal team to align on exact wording?

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines - internal legal thoughts

Priyom / Marissa — read through Vellum's redlines. Key legal points and risks: 

1) Absolute "no training" language is customer-friendly but operationally tricky. We can agree to "no training on Customer Data or Outputs without Customer's written consent." That gives Vellum the control they want while allowing future negotiated exceptions.

2) Feedback license: propose the following guardrails — limited purpose (to improve service quality and safety), non-exclusive, royalty-free, and limited to aggregated or de-identified signals. No right to include identifiable Customer Data or verbatim Outputs into training corpora. Also add a timebound retention (e.g., 12 months) for non-anonymized telemetry used for debugging.

3) Outputs vs Derivatives: Vellum wants "ownership of Outputs (and derivatives)". We should accept ownership of Outputs for customer-generated content, but reserve our IP in the underlying models and in any model-level improvements derived from aggregated signals. Suggest: "Customer owns Outputs; Redwood retains all rights in and to the Service and Models. Any improvements to the Models based solely on aggregated, de-identified telemetry shall be owned by Redwood."

4) Exceptions: security/fraud/abuse detection and compliance monitoring need a carve-out. Those uses should be allowed (with strict minimization) and logged in audit trails.

Next steps: I'll produce redline language for the MSA and a short one-pager the sales team can share. We should get product confirmation (Laura) on feasibility of the telemetry retention and anonymization timelines.

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redlines - commercial proposal and path forward

Hi Sara — appreciate the candid asks. To move the deal forward, here's a commercial/legal compromise Redwood can sign up to: 

Proposed bullets (summary):
- Outputs: Vellum retains ownership of all Outputs created from its inputs and prompts. Redwood will not assert rights over those Outputs.
- Training: Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve foundation models without prior written consent from Vellum.
- Feedback license: Vellum grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer Feedback (defined narrowly) solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Redwood Service, provided that such use excludes incorporating identifiable Customer Data or verbatim Outputs into model training datasets. Aggregated or de-identified telemetry may be used for model tuning and safety improvements.
- Security/Monitoring: Redwood may use telemetry for abuse detection, safety monitoring and debugging; such uses will be minimized, logged, and subject to retention limits (proposal: 90 days for raw logs, 12 months for anonymized diagnostic traces).

I've attached a marked OrderForm_v2_marked.docx and a short redlines-summary.xlsx that maps each customer request to proposed Redwood language and rationale. If this looks acceptable, we can prepare a short legal call with Andrew (if Vellum wants outside counsel involved) and finish the MSA + Order Form redline.

Action item: Sara — can you confirm whether Vellum requires revocable licenses or any post-termination restrictions beyond the training prohibition? That will help Karthik finalize wording.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: MSA redlines - outside counsel comments

Marissa / team — representing Vellum. Couple of points from our side after reviewing Redwood's proposal: 

- Perpetual license for Feedback: Vellum prefers that any license to use Customer Feedback for product improvement be revocable on reasonable notice and/or limited in duration (not perpetual). We propose a 24-month license term and an opt-out mechanism for customers who want to restrict ongoing use.

- Notification & Audit: Vellum requests a notification obligation before Redwood uses any Customer Data for aggregated training and an audit right limited in scope and frequency (e.g., once per 12 months).

- Escrow/Proof: For high-risk customers (PHI-heavy), Vellum may require a short side-letter confirming no training use and specifying technical safeguards; we can provide suggested language.

I've attached a short draft clause (vellum_feedback_clause_draft.docx) that captures these points. Happy to jump on a call to finalize.

Andrew Byrne
